Kuponlu İhraçlar: Refers to the periodic interest payment of a security. For example, for a security with a nominal value of 100,000 TL, paying 5% coupon interest every 3 months, with a maturity of 1 year, an interest (coupon) payment of 5,000 TL is made to its investor every 3 months, and at the end of 1 year its principal, 100,000 TL, is paid.
Kurumsal bağımsızlık: The determination, by law and away from political pressure, of the tenures of central banks' senior executives and of their appointment and working rules.
Kurumsal kalite: The conceptual measure showing collectively the properties in a country such as its form of governance, the rule of law, property rights, political stability, bureaucratic effectiveness, the prevention of corruption, and the accountability of those governing.
Kurumsal nüfus: The population living under the roof of an institution or establishment, such as university dormitories, training hostels, nursing homes, hospitals, prisons and barracks.
Kurumsallaşma: The transaction of bringing an institution, an organization or a business to a structure enabling it to continue and develop its activities without being dependent on individuals.
Kuzey Anadolu Kalkınma Ajansı: All publication rights of this document belong to the Directorate General for Development Agencies of the Ministry of Industry and Technology. Private sector investments hold an important place in the country's development. For investments contribute in many respects, such as raising national income, increasing production and employment, developing exports, raising the accumulation of technological knowledge and tax revenues, invigorating the economy and developing the markets
Kâr: Or in short Π: the difference between the total revenue obtained from an economic activity and the total cost incurred for it. Also, the incomes such as the profit shares companies distribute to their capital owners, or undistributed company profits.
Kâr maksimizasyonu: The selection of the quantity of production that will maximize total profit, with revenues and costs given.
Kötü mal: Products that bring harm to economic units and whose price in the market is negative.
Kümelenme: The working model in which producer firms operating in the same or a similar line of business, geographically close to one another, in cooperation and competition with one another, come together with the firms and institutions supporting them.
Küreselleşme: Countries and societies coming closer to one another economically, politically and culturally.
Kısa dönem: In the microeconomic context, the conceptual time interval in which entry into or exit from the market is not possible and at least one production factor is fixed. In the macroeconomic context, it is the conceptual time interval in which prices and wages are fixed and production factors can show limited mobility among regions and sectors.
Kısa dönem Phillips eğrisi: Or in short SRPC: a graphical tool showing the relationship between the unemployment and inflation rates when only the data belonging to the past and the present are taken into account.
Kısa dönem toplam arz eğrisi: Or in short SRAS: a graphical tool showing the short-run relationship between the general price level and the quantity of aggregate supply, all else being constant.
Kısa Vadeli Dış Borç Stoku: The balance of the current, unconditional obligations requiring principal and/or interest payment(s) to be made within one year from the date of use, that have had their use realized as of any date and that the resident persons in an economy owe to non-residents. It consists of the short-term portion of the deposits at the CBRT, the short-term credits of banks and other sectors (including bonds issued abroad), the short-term trade credits of other sectors, the foreign currency deposit account (DTH) showing the foreign currency deposits of resident real and legal persons abroad (excluding banks) at resident domestic banks, the bank deposits showing the foreign currency deposits of banks resident abroad at resident domestic banks, and the deposit items showing the Turkish lira deposits of resident real and legal persons abroad (including banks) at resident domestic banks.
Kıtlık: Or excess demand: the situation in which the quantity demanded in the market exceeds the quantity supplied.
Leniency Programs: The programs regulating the procedures and principles of not fining, or granting reductions in the fines to be imposed on, those cooperating with the competition authority with the aim of uncovering cartels. In Turkish competition law, the provision on this subject is made with the Leniency Regulation.
Lerner endeksi: Or in short L: the market power measure calculated by dividing the difference between a product's price and its marginal cost by the price.
LIBOR: In the London Interbank Money Market, the interest rate applied by highly reputable banks in their lending transactions to one another over the base currencies (US dollar, euro, British pound, Japanese yen and Swiss franc).
Likidite Desteği Kredisi: The Turkish lira credit support provided by the CBRT, in the event that uncertainty and insecurity form in the banking system and fund withdrawals accelerate, to the banks regarding which uncertainty and insecurity have formed but that have the ability to pay, in the form of advances with one-month maturities and for a maximum of one year, against collateral in an amount to cover the fund withdrawals, limited to twice their equity.
Likidite Senetleri: A monetary policy instrument with the property of short-term bills, used with the aim of increasing the effectiveness of monetary policy and regulating the liquidity in the market (withdrawing the excess liquidity). According to Article 52 of the CBRT Law, the CBRT can issue liquidity bills with maturities not exceeding 91 days, in its own name and for its own account.
Lira başına marjinal fayda: The additional utility brought by spending one more unit of money for a certain good or service.
Lira başına marjinal ürün: The additional product brought by spending one more unit of money for a certain production factor.
Lisanslı Depoculuk: The facility providing the services of preserving agricultural products in healthy conditions and storing them for commercial purposes, within the scope of the Licensed Warehousing of Agricultural Products Law No. 5300. Lobbying: the activity of influencing the decisions given by governments or international organizations. Mineral Exploration Investment: the investment directed at extracting a mineral. Mineral Processing Investment: the investment directed at processing a mineral. Return to Origin: the returning of a good to the place it came from (the country of exit/where the trade was conducted)
LM eğrisi: A graphical tool showing the relationship between total production and the interest rate when the money market in the economy is in equilibrium.
Londra Bankalararası Faiz Oranı: Or in short LIBOR: the interest rate banks pay one another in the London money market for their daily uncollateralized borrowings.
Lorenz eğrisi: A graphical tool showing the relationship between the percentage shares of the households in a country according to population and the percentage share these households receive from income.
Lüks mal: Products whose demand in the market increases at a higher rate when the average income level rises.
Macaulay süresi: The maturity-weighted average present-value time of a bond's cash flows: for each t, the ratio of the sum of t·PV to the price; in years.
Mahreç İşareti: The names defining the products originating from a locality, region or country with determined geographical boundaries, identified with this geographical area in respect of a distinctive quality, reputation or other characteristics, at least one of whose production, processing and other operations is carried out within the boundaries of the determined geographical area.
Makroekonomi: The main branch of economics that takes the decision-makers in the economy as a whole and examines their collective behavior.
Makroekonomi politikası: The rules and practices the state uses with the aim of managing various macroeconomic magnitudes, chiefly national income and inflation.
Makroekonomik popülizm: Politicians' pursuing, in the short run, unsustainable expansionary fiscal policies with the aim of appearing attractive to the public, at the cost of the economy suffering harm in the long run.
Maktu vergi: The tax taken as fixed on the unit of the object subject to the tax.
Mal para: General payment instruments in the form of goods having a concrete use value.
Mal ve hizmetler hesabı: The heading in the balance of payments showing foreign trade revenues and expenditures.
Mali (Finansal) Kuruluşlar: Contains the institutional units consisting of independent legal persons and market producers whose fundamental function is to produce financial services.
Mali (Finansal) Olmayan Kuruluşlar: Contains the institutional units consisting of independent legal persons and market producers whose fundamental function is to produce non-financial services and products.
Mali yıl: The period of implementation of the public budget; in Türkiye it begins on 1 January and ends on 31 December.
Maliye Politikası: The shaping by governments of their methods of collecting revenue, spending and borrowing, with the aim of realizing certain aims such as employment, growth and inflation.
Maliyet-fayda çözümlemesi: The decision-making method examining mathematically the positive and negative outcomes that different preferences will bring.

Marginal Revenue: The extra revenue obtained when sales increase by one unit.
Marjinal değer: Or in short MV: the additional benefit brought to the monopsonist buyer by purchasing one more unit of a product.
Marjinal dönüşüm oranı: Or in short MRT: the opportunity cost, in terms of another product, of producing one more unit of a certain product.
Marjinal gelir: Or in short MR: the additional revenue brought by making one more unit of sales.
Marjinal gider: Or in short MC: the additional cost incurred to produce one more unit.
Marjinal harcama: Or in short ME: the additional expenditure made to purchase one more unit of a product.
Marjinal ikame oranı: Or in short MRS: the amount of one product to be given up in order to consume more of another, keeping total utility unchanged.
Marjinal ithalat eğilimi: Or in short MPM: the change seen in the quantity of imports when total income in an economy increases by one unit.
